record.paper_title: Open problems from the 12th International Conference on Fuzzy Set Theory and Its Applications
record.original_question: Generalize the quantitative-logic setup from the case where the truth-degree set is the real unit interval or a finite subset of it to the case where the truth-degree set is an arbitrary lattice. In particular, determine how formulas, truth functions, and meta-degree assignments should be formulated in that lattice-valued setting.

evidence.quote: Problem 8.3 (S. Gottwald). How to generalize this setting for the case that the truth degree set is a lattice?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In quantitative logic over many-valued propositional calculi, one fixes a truth-degree set W (classically W = [0,1] or a finite chain W_n ⊂ [0,1]) together with a system of truth functions interpreting the connectives (e.g. a continuous t-norm and its residuum). For each propositional formula φ(p_1,…,p_n) one obtains an induced truth function φ̄: W^n → W. Given a probability measure (or a uniformly distributed counting measure in the finite case) on W^n, one then defines the "truth degree" τ(φ) ∈ [0,1] of φ as the expected value (integral / average) of φ̄ over all valuations, and uses these meta-degrees to define a logic pseudo-metric ρ(φ,ψ) = τ(φ ↔ ψ-complement) on the set of formulas, with which approximate reasoning, divergence degree, and consistency degree of theories are studied.

Problem. Develop an analogous quantitative-logic framework in the case where the truth-degree set is replaced by an arbitrary (bounded) lattice L (not necessarily linearly ordered, not necessarily embedded in [0,1]). Specifically:

(a) Specify a suitable class of formulas and a system of L-valued truth functions interpreting the propositional connectives over L (for instance via residuated lattice or complete lattice operations).

(b) Define an appropriate notion of "meta-degree" or truth degree τ(φ) of a formula φ in this L-valued setting, replacing the integral-with-respect-to-a-probability-measure construction available on [0,1]; in particular, identify what mathematical structure on L (measure, capacity, averaging operator, lattice-valued integral such as a Sugeno-type integral, or otherwise) plays the role of the uniform/Lebesgue measure used in the real-valued case, and what codomain (the lattice L itself, [0,1], or another structure) the meta-degree should take values in.

(c) Using this notion, define and study the induced logic (pseudo-)metric or similarity on the set of formulas, and verify that the basic properties known in the [0,1]-valued case (such as well-definedness up to logical equivalence, compatibility with connectives, and a reasonable theory of consistency/divergence degrees of theories) carry over or determine precisely which properties fail.

Provide such a framework, or prove obstructions showing that no satisfactory generalization exists for general lattices L.
artifact.status_search_result: Several works have addressed lattice-valued truth-degree theory (e.g. truth degrees over MV-algebras, generalized truth degrees in n-valued NM-logic, truth degrees in nonlinear/quintuple lattice-valued Gödel logic), giving partial generalizations beyond the real unit interval. However, a fully general framework for quantitative logic over an arbitrary lattice as truth-degree set does not appear to be established; results so far cover specific algebraic classes of lattices.

status_evidence.title: Lattice-Valued Truth Degree in Łukasiewicz Propositional Fuzzy Logic
status_evidence.snippet: Defines formula truth degree on MV-algebra (a bounded distributive lattice) as lattice-valued truth degree generalizing the [0,1] case.
status_evidence.claim: Partial generalization to MV-algebra-valued (lattice-valued) truth degrees exists.

status_evidence.title: The generalized truth degree of quantitative logic in n-valued NM-logic
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized truth degrees in n-valued NM-logic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative-logic truth degrees have been extended to particular finite lattice-based logics.

status_evidence.title: Truth degree of formula in 4-valued Gödel nonlinear lattice logic
status_evidence.snippet: Truth degrees in a nonlinear (lattice) Gödel logic.
status_evidence.claim: Truth degrees have been defined for some non-linearly-ordered lattice truth-value sets.
